findings.finding: A status carrying ANSI (pi's documented 'themed colors' example) renders its escape sequences as visible text — ' [32m● [0m ok' — because the format language collapses ESC in every datum value, a rule that predates this change and is right for every other datum but was never reconciled with a datum that is styled text by convention. Reproduced with the real resolver. The route: keeping the colour would revise the ratified collapse rule and let one datum's SGR leak into the cell's own style and pad (the trap AGENTS.md names), so the colour is stripped and the cell's `style` owns the colour, as it does for every other instrument. Stripping is the instrument's job (variables arrive already formatted), and pi-tui's stripTerminalSequences is the existing helper — a host package import, which the layout spec and imports.mjs allow in an instrument file. No new mechanism. Measured: stripTerminalSequences("\x1b[32m●\x1b[0m ok") === "● ok"; it also removes OSC 8 links, leaving their text. Joel can overrule in favour of keeping colour; that would be a design change to the collapse rule, not a fix.

findings.finding: defaultForm has no reader. The bare variable's rendering is variables.<name>, and path points both it and byName.base at one function, so the behaviour is right and pinned ($path === $path|base, tests/instrument.test.ts:194) — but the default is now stated in two places and the declared one does nothing, while AGENTS.md instructs authors to set it. A future instrument setting defaultForm to a form other than its variables entry would change nothing and nobody would be told. One home for the fact: variables.<name> is the default a bare variable hands out; byName lists the named forms. Removing the field is the smallest fix and adds no mechanism; wiring it as a consumer would make resolveFormat consult two tables for one value.

requirements.evidence: Reproduced at 04c3a78 with the real parseFormat/resolveFormat over the shipped status declaration and a status of "\x1b[32m●\x1b[0m ok": the cell text is " [32m● [0m ok". Cause: resolveFormat passes every datum value through collapse (format.ts), which maps ESC to a space — the ratified rule for datum text (living spec 'Content that would span more than one line'; tests/format.test.ts:196 'collapse runs before styling so data ESC becomes a space'). pi's example status-line extension sets themed colours and pi's own footer keeps them (footer.js sanitizeStatusText does not touch ESC; truncateToWidth is ANSI-aware). The status instrument is the first datum that routinely carries ANSI, so this is a defect this change introduced: the instrument cannot show the datum it was shipped to show. Valid blocker.
